ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square based pyramid (that is symmetrical) is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value of $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: a cube with side length labeled ℓ=10 cm placed on horizontal ground, with a symmetric square-base pyramid placed exactly on top; the base of the pyramid is completely aligned with the top face of the cube. According to the specified method, regard the pyramid as a regular square pyramid with base edge ℓ and height also ℓ. Therefore the cube volume is ℓ^3, and the pyramid volume is ℓ^3/3; the two have the same density, so if the cube mass is M, then the pyramid mass is m=M/3. The cube is instantaneously given a horizontal initial velocity v, while the pyramid is initially still stationary relative to the ground, so sliding friction first occurs between the two. The pyramid receives a horizontal friction force of magnitude μmg, with direction causing it to accelerate, so a_p=μg. The cube, on one hand, receives the ground friction force μ(M+m)g, and on the other hand receives the reverse friction force μmg from the pyramid on it, so the magnitude of the cube's deceleration is [μ(M+m)g+μmg]/M. Substituting m=M/3 gives a_c=-(μ(4M/3)g+μ(M/3)g)/M=-(5/3)μg. The relative acceleration is A=a_p-a_c=μg+(5/3)μg=(8/3)μg, used to eliminate the initial relative velocity v. The relative sliding distance is d=v^2/(2A)=v^2/[2(8/3)μg]=3v^2/(16μg). In order to make the allowed relative displacement maximum, take the initial velocity direction along the diagonal direction of the square top face. The limiting condition for the pyramid base to remain parallel to the cube top face is that the projection of its center of mass is still within the cube top face; along the diagonal direction, the distance from the center to the corner point is d_max=ℓ/√2. Let 3v^2/(16μg)=ℓ/√2, obtaining v=sqrt(16μgℓ/(3√2)). Substituting μ=0.3, ℓ=0.10 m, taking g≈10 m/s^2, v≈sqrt(16×0.3×10×0.10/(3√2))≈1.07 m/s.

method.method_draft: Direct force-and-kinematics route. Read the stack as a cube of side l=0.10 m with a right square pyramid of matching base and intended height l, so the pyramid mass is m=M/3 because the densities are equal. Since the cube alone is given initial speed v while the pyramid initially lags, use kinetic friction during the slip phase. Friction on the pyramid is +mu m g, so a_p=mu g. The cube is slowed by floor friction mu(M+m)g and by the top-interface friction mu m g, so a_c=-(mu(M+m)g+mu m g)/M=-(5/3)mu g. Hence the relative acceleration opposing the initial relative velocity is A=a_p-a_c=(8/3)mu g, and the relative sliding distance before the two bodies acquire the same velocity is d=v^2/(2A)=3v^2/(16 mu g). To maximize the allowed speed, choose the initial direction along a diagonal of the square top; the pyramid remains untipped/parallel as long as the projection of its center stays inside the cube top, allowing maximum relative shift d_max=l/sqrt(2). Set 3v^2/(16 mu g)=l/sqrt(2), giving v=sqrt(16 mu g l/(3 sqrt(2)))≈1.07 m/s using g≈10 m/s^2.

method.method_draft: Relative-coordinate work-energy route. From the geometry, take the cube mass as M and the matching square pyramid mass as m=M/3. Model only the slipping stage after the cube receives speed v, using the relative coordinate x = position of cube top minus position of pyramid base center. The initial relative kinetic energy is (1/2) m_red v^2 with reduced mass m_red=Mm/(M+m)=M/4. The relative motion is opposed by a constant effective generalized friction force F_eff=m_red A, where the relative deceleration from the contact and floor frictions is A=(8/3)mu g; equivalently F_eff=(M/4)(8/3)mu g=(2/3)mu M g. Thus the relative slide before relative motion ceases is x=(1/2 m_red v^2)/F_eff=3v^2/(16 mu g). The geometric no-tipping/no-rotation limit is largest if the cube is launched along the top-face diagonal, so the pyramid center may move at most l/sqrt(2) before leaving the square support. Equating 3v^2/(16 mu g)=l/sqrt(2) yields v≈1.07 m/s.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description first: The attached figures show a cube with a symmetric square-based pyramid sitting directly on its top face. The pyramid base is aligned with the cube top square, and the cube side/top edge is labeled l = 10 cm. The pyramid apex is above the square base center, with hidden edges shown dotted.

Reasoning following the assigned relative-coordinate work-energy route: Let the cube mass be M. Since the pyramid has the same base area as the cube top and, from the geometry used in the method, volume one third of the cube volume, its mass is m = M/3. Use the relative coordinate x = position of the cube top minus position of the pyramid base center along the launch direction. Initially, after the cube is given speed v, the pyramid is at rest, so the initial relative speed is v. The reduced mass is m_red = Mm/(M + m) = M(M/3)/(4M/3) = M/4, so the initial relative kinetic energy is (1/2)(M/4)v^2.

During slipping, friction at the cube-pyramid contact and at the floor produces a constant relative deceleration A = (8/3)mu g. Equivalently, the effective generalized friction force opposing the relative coordinate is F_eff = m_red A = (M/4)(8/3)mu g = (2/3)mu M g. Therefore the relative sliding distance before relative motion ceases is
x = [(1/2)m_red v^2]/F_eff = [(1/2)(M/4)v^2]/[(2/3)mu M g] = 3v^2/(16 mu g).

To keep the pyramid base parallel to the cube top, the pyramid must not tip during this sliding. The most favorable launch direction is along a diagonal of the square top face, because then the pyramid center can move the greatest distance before the support condition is lost. That maximum allowed relative displacement is x_max = l/sqrt(2). Set the stopping slide equal to this limit:
3v^2/(16 mu g) = l/sqrt(2), so v = sqrt(16 mu g l/(3 sqrt(2))).

With l = 0.10 m, mu = 0.3, and the intended g approximation, this gives v about 1.07 m/s.

raw_record.original_question: A symmetrical square-based pyramid is standing on top of a cube with side length $\ell=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ such that their square faces perfectly line up. The cube is initially standing still on flat ground, and both objects have the same uniform density. The coefficient of friction between every surface is the same value, $\mu=0.3$. The cube is then given an initial speed $v$ in some direction parallel to the floor. What is the maximum possible value of $v$ such that the base of the pyramid will always remain parallel to the top of the cube? Answer in meters per second.
raw_record.final_cot: The image shows: a cube with side length labeled ℓ=10 cm placed on horizontal ground, with a symmetric square-base pyramid placed exactly on top; the base of the pyramid is completely aligned with the top face of the cube. According to the specified method, regard the pyramid as a regular square pyramid with base edge ℓ and height also ℓ. Therefore the cube volume is ℓ^3, and the pyramid volume is ℓ^3/3; the two have the same density, so if the cube mass is M, then the pyramid mass is m=M/3. The cube is instantaneously given a horizontal initial velocity v, while the pyramid is initially still stationary relative to the ground, so sliding friction first occurs between the two. The pyramid receives a horizontal friction force of magnitude μmg, with direction causing it to accelerate, so a_p=μg. The cube, on one hand, receives the ground friction force μ(M+m)g, and on the other hand receives the reverse friction force μmg from the pyramid on it, so the magnitude of the cube's deceleration is [μ(M+m)g+μmg]/M. Substituting m=M/3 gives a_c=-(μ(4M/3)g+μ(M/3)g)/M=-(5/3)μg. The relative acceleration is A=a_p-a_c=μg+(5/3)μg=(8/3)μg, used to eliminate the initial relative velocity v. The relative sliding distance is d=v^2/(2A)=v^2/[2(8/3)μg]=3v^2/(16μg). In order to make the allowed relative displacement maximum, take the initial velocity direction along the diagonal direction of the square top face. The limiting condition for the pyramid base to remain parallel to the cube top face is that the projection of its center of mass is still within the cube top face; along the diagonal direction, the distance from the center to the corner point is d_max=ℓ/√2. Let 3v^2/(16μg)=ℓ/√2, obtaining v=sqrt(16μgℓ/(3√2)). Substituting μ=0.3, ℓ=0.10 m, taking g≈10 m/s^2, v≈sqrt(16×0.3×10×0.10/(3√2))≈1.07 m/s.
